title: Alfred Wegener and the Broken Jigsaw of Pangaea
summary: Gazing at the uncanny fit between South America and Africa and matching fossil fern and reptile beds across oceans, a German meteorologist braved arctic blizzards and fierce academic scorn to prove all landmasses once formed one giant supercontinent: Pangaea.
keywords: Alfred Wegener and the Broken Jigsaw of Pangaea
The Theory of Continental Drift and the Supercontinent Pangaea
full_text:
In 1915 CE, the frontiers of human understanding were transformed through the indomitable persistence of Alfred Wegener.

At the time, the reigning scientific establishment in the field of Geophysics & Plate Tectonics was constrained by orthodox paradigms that could no longer account for emerging experimental anomalies. While many researchers looked past these discrepancies or dismissed them as instrument artifacts, Alfred Wegener recognized that the anomaly was itself a beacon pointing toward an undiscovered law of nature.

Working from primary documentation recorded in *Die Entstehung der Kontinente und Ozeane (The Origin of Continents and Oceans, 1915)* (Friedrich Vieweg & Sohn, Braunschweig; Chapters 1–3), the breakthrough emerged through painstaking methodology. Every alternative hypothesis was systematically tested, isolated, and eliminated under rigorous controls.

Gazing at the uncanny fit between South America and Africa and matching fossil fern and reptile beds across oceans, a German meteorologist braved arctic blizzards and fierce academic scorn to prove all landmasses once formed one giant supercontinent: Pangaea.

The discovery of The Theory of Continental Drift and the Supercontinent Pangaea did not merely answer a localized puzzle; it triggered a profound paradigm shift across Geophysics & Plate Tectonics. Today, its principles form the bedrock of modern empirical science, reminding every student that progress is forged when courageous curiosity meets disciplined observation.
